moments.title: Why use standard form?
moments.text: Write very large or very small values compactly as a coefficient multiplied by a power of 10.

moments.title: A large number
moments.text: Moving the decimal point five places gives $457000=4.57\times10^5$.

moments.title: A small number
moments.text: A positive value smaller than 1 has a negative power of 10.

moments.title: The required form
moments.text: Use $a\times10^k$, where $1\leq a<10$ and $k$ is an integer.

ican.text: I can convert positive numbers between decimal notation and standard form.
I can calculate with numbers in standard form and give the answer in standard form.
I can round an answer in standard form to a specified number of significant figures.

ku.text: Standard form is $a\times10^k$, where $1\leq a<10$ and $k$ is an integer. For negative numbers, put a minus sign in front of the standard-form magnitude.
For a positive number greater than or equal to 10, $k$ is positive. For a positive number between 0 and 1, $k$ is negative. Numbers from 1 up to 10 have $k=0$.
For multiplication, multiply coefficients and add exponents. For division, divide coefficients and subtract exponents. Renormalize the result if the coefficient is outside $[1,10)$.
To add or subtract, first express the quantities using the same power of 10, then combine coefficients.

misc.better: The coefficient must be less than 10. Write $3.24\times10^6$.
The original positive number is less than 1, so $0.0042=4.2\times10^{-3}$.

terms.text: Give the coefficient and power of 10, with the coefficient in the required range.
Use the calculator and report the requested accuracy, keeping extra digits during working.

formula.text: Use the exponent laws when multiplying or dividing powers of 10. Check the formula booklet for the exact permitted rules.

worked.prompt: A bacterium has a mass of $0.00000000000274$ g. A sample contains exactly $3\times10^6$ bacteria of this mass.

parts.label: (a)
parts.q: Write the mass of one bacterium in standard form.

parts.label: (b)
parts.q: Find the total mass in standard form.

kq.model: Its coefficient is 24, outside the standard-form interval. The equivalent standard form is $2.4\times10^4$.
